findings.title: Interrupted save is described as definitely not saved

evidence.detail: nhs-confirmation-not-saved says “The schedule was not saved”.
The only stated evidence is an interrupted connection before confirmation; the draft summary later says “Save not confirmed”.

findings.proposed_change: Use an uncertainty heading such as “We could not confirm the save” and keep the advice to inspect saved schedules before retrying. Alternatively, if demonstrating a confirmed rejection, change the scenario to an explicitly rejected persistence response. Update the example title/description to match the chosen state.
acceptance: The heading, description, body and summary all distinguish an unconfirmed save from a known rejected save.
The specimen does not assert that nothing changed or encourage an unqualified duplicate request.

findings.title: Missing information and failed actions use overgeneral state wording

evidence.detail: The table maps any sensor with no current reading to “Reading unavailable”, omitting unknown or retained/stale readings.
The table maps every failed device command to “The device did not respond”; a request may instead be explicitly rejected.
nhs-pattern-review-guidance says availability describes whether HA can currently reach each entity, equating entity state availability with network reachability.
nhs-identifier-error says “No available entity matches this ID” even though the scenario is a misspelled/not-found identifier; this conflates matching with current availability.

findings.proposed_change: Split the recovery table into evidence-specific unknown, unavailable, retained-old-value, rejected-request and no-confirmation cases. Describe availability as whether a usable entity state is supplied, not proof of physical reachability. In the identifier specimen, use “No entity matches this ID” within the authorised scope and keep unavailable-but-matched entities as a separate case.
acceptance: An unknown reading, unavailable entity and old retained value have distinct wording without being rendered as zero/off/offline.
An explicit rejection does not say the device failed to respond.
An unavailable matched identifier is not described as absent or misspelled.

findings.title: Rename specimen promises a local change that it does not perform

evidence.detail: nhs-question-modal states “Rename changes only the displayed label in this preview”.
The generic demo submit handler only changes the local status text; it does not update the displayed control label or persist the entered name.

findings.proposed_change: Keep the reference demonstration local and change its explanation to say that submitting shows local feedback but does not rename the preview or a Home Assistant entity. If actual preview renaming is desired later, specify and implement that bounded behaviour explicitly rather than leaving the claim unsupported.
acceptance: The visible instruction and final feedback accurately describe what the current submit handler changes.
No wording claims a saved name or changed entity unless that operation is actually implemented and verified.

findings.title: Written BSL companion guide invents a theme preview/save step

evidence.detail: The written theme guide says “Preview the selection before saving”.
The documented palette flow applies the generated theme when either control changes.
Both controls call apply() on change; the actual component has no Preview or Save button.

findings.proposed_change: Describe the actual Colour palette and Use muted colours controls and say that choosing them applies the appearance through the native theme flow. Remove the nonexistent Preview/Save step. Preserve the honest statement that no BSL translation is commissioned or available.
acceptance: Every named step maps to an existing control and the described order matches immediate selection behaviour.
Future signed content would be commissioned from the corrected, versioned written instructions rather than this obsolete step.

findings.title: Calendar specimens omit the time zone and selected date range

evidence.detail: The timed appointment is “09:00” on 12 November 2026, with no declared zone or offset in its table/caption.
The empty state says “selected week” but provides no dates identifying that week.

findings.proposed_change: Give the synthetic agenda an explicit example time zone and give the empty-week heading/caption an actual labelled example date range. Keep the all-day event as a date-based event rather than converting it to midnight.
acceptance: A reader can identify the example timed appointment’s zone without assuming the browser or household zone.
A reader can identify the selected empty period from visible text.
Synthetic status and native calendar ownership remain explicit.
